title: NSAIDs at 20 weeks or later in pregnancy

csc.title: NSAIDs in pregnancy at 20 weeks or later
requiredMonitoring: amniotic fluid monitoring if NSAID treatment extends beyond 48 hours
csc.recommendedActionTemplate: Review {patient}'s NSAID exposure ({medications}) in pregnancy. Stop or substitute when clinically appropriate and consider amniotic-fluid monitoring if use is necessary.
csc.rationale: NSAID use at or after 20 weeks gestation can cause fetal renal dysfunction and oligohydramnios.

patient.name: Mrs. Clarence Reinger
patient.visitTitle: Prenatal intake visit — initial obstetric evaluation

cases.rationale: Mrs. Reinger is in early first-trimester pregnancy, well below the 20-week gestational threshold at which NSAID risk (fetal renal dysfunction/oligohydramnios) applies. She reports only occasional unspecified OTC headache analgesia with no confirmed NSAID use, and she was already counseled to clear any OTC medication with the office first.
cases.monitorNote: At the next prenatal visit, ask specifically which OTC analgesic she uses for headaches (ibuprofen/Advil, naproxen/Aleve vs. acetaminophen). Re-assess NSAID use as gestation approaches 20 weeks; from 20 weeks onward the FDA alert becomes applicable and NSAIDs should be avoided, with amniotic fluid monitoring if any NSAID use exceeds 48 hours.
cases.draftedAction: No action required today. At the next scheduled prenatal visit (in 4 weeks), the clinician should ask Mrs. Reinger to name the specific OTC product she uses for headaches and document it; if it is an NSAID (ibuprofen/Advil, naproxen/Aleve), counsel her to switch to acetaminophen as the preferred analgesic in pregnancy. Preemptively advise that NSAIDs must be avoided from 20 weeks gestation onward due to risk of fetal kidney problems and low amniotic fluid. Reinforce the existing instruction to contact the office before starting any new OTC medication.

cases.monitorNote: Re-check at each prenatal visit whether she has started any OTC pain relievers for back pain; the alert becomes actionable at 20 weeks gestation (approximately mid-October 2024 based on late-May LMP). Counsel proactively before that point that ibuprofen (Advil/Motrin) and naproxen (Aleve) should be avoided from 20 weeks onward.
cases.draftedAction: No action required today; do not start or stop any medication based on this alert. At today's or the next visit, the clinician should preemptively counsel Ms. Thiel that OTC NSAIDs (ibuprofen/Advil/Motrin, naproxen/Aleve) must be avoided at and after 20 weeks of pregnancy due to fetal kidney risk, and recommend acetaminophen as the preferred analgesic for her scoliosis-related back pain. Ask specifically about OTC analgesic use at each subsequent prenatal visit, especially as back pain increases with gestational age.

cases.monitorNote: Re-screen for OTC NSAID use (ibuprofen/Advil/Motrin, naproxen/Aleve) at each prenatal visit and specifically re-check when the patient reaches 20 weeks gestation (approximately mid-December 2019). If NSAID use is identified at or beyond 20 weeks, apply the alert: stop or substitute the NSAID and consider amniotic-fluid monitoring if use exceeds 48 hours.
cases.draftedAction: At the next prenatal visit (in ~4 weeks), counsel Mrs. Rau to avoid OTC NSAIDs (ibuprofen/Advil/Motrin, naproxen/Aleve) throughout pregnancy and especially at or after 20 weeks, recommending acetaminophen as the preferred analgesic when needed. Ask explicitly about OTC pain reliever use at each visit, since these drugs are available without a prescription and may not appear in the medication list. No action is required today beyond this preemptive counseling; do not issue an NSAID alert now, as she is at 10 weeks with no documented or reported exposure.

patient.name: Ms. Melodee Bobette Satterfield
patient.visitTitle: Prenatal intake visit — first pregnancy with chronic pain

cases.rationale: Ms. Satterfield is pregnant at approximately 10 weeks, below the 20-week gestational threshold at which the NSAID alert applies, and there is no evidence of NSAID exposure — her chronic pain is managed exclusively with opioids and she explicitly denied other substances. The alert becomes potentially applicable around gestational week 20 (~late May 2026), and her upcoming opioid taper creates a plausible pathway to future OTC NSAID self-treatment.
cases.monitorNote: No NSAID exposure today; alert becomes applicable at 20 weeks gestation (~late May 2026, given ~10 weeks on 2026-03-21). At each prenatal visit — and especially as the opioid taper progresses — ask specifically about OTC NSAID use (Advil, Motrin, Aleve, ibuprofen, naproxen). Re-verify no NSAID use before and at the 20-week visit.
cases.draftedAction: Counsel Ms. Satterfield preemptively today or at the next contact that OTC NSAIDs (ibuprofen/Advil/Motrin, naproxen/Aleve) must be avoided from 20 weeks gestation onward due to risk of fetal kidney problems and low amniotic fluid, and that acetaminophen (within safe limits, noting her combination hydrocodone/acetaminophen tablets) is the preferred OTC analgesic. Ensure the pain specialist coordinating her opioid taper knows not to recommend NSAIDs as a substitute during the taper. Do not stop or change her current opioid regimen abruptly; continue the planned gradual taper. Ask specifically about OTC analgesic use at each prenatal visit.
